summary: Excess 429s during nightly billing-sweep capacity refresh (mid-window refill anomaly)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a recurring spike of 429 responses between 00:10–00:25 UTC during their nightly billing/usage sweep. The spike correlates to a platform-side token refill event that runs as part of billing finalization. Impact: several dozen production clients (on the customer's dedicated pool) saw transient failures for short-lived streaming sessions and concurrent API calls.

Impact:
- ~18% increased error rate (429) for the customer's API keys during the 15-minute window.
- Client-side retries cause additional amplified traffic leading to cascading backpressure.
- Customer has scheduled bulk warmups at 00:05 UTC which may be interacting with the refill.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (DocuSift dedicated tenant) in us-east
- Production traffic pattern: many short-lived streaming sessions + periodic bulk warmup tasks nightly

Desired outcome:
- Understand why global refill (billing sweep) causes mid-window token accounting to temporarily over-throttle the tenant despite available quota afterward.
- Provide a mitigation path or config guidance to avoid production impact during midnight maintenance windows.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have a dedicated tenant with scheduled warmups at 00:05 UTC (many short streaming sessions).
2) Ensure tenant has a per-tenant quota with a refill aligned to daily billing sweep at 00:15 UTC.
3) Run concurrent short streaming sessions and several bulk generation calls between 00:05–00:20 UTC.
4) Observe 429s concentrated around 00:10–00:25 UTC window.

Note: Customer provided an automated replay trace of the pattern for March 8–10 which reproduces the spike every night.
logs:
Selected sample from edge-gateway logs (us-east) aggregated for SUP-801999 window:
[2026-03-09T00:09:58Z] key=ds-prod-01 conn=start session_id=abc123 route=/v1/chat tokens=0
[2026-03-09T00:10:12Z] key=ds-prod-01 response=429 reason=token_quota_exhausted window_id=2026-03-09T00:00
[2026-03-09T00:10:13Z] key=ds-prod-01 response=429 reason=token_quota_exhausted window_id=2026-03-09T00:00
[2026-03-09T00:11:45Z] billing-agent EVENT=refill_start tenant=docusize window=2026-03-09T00:00
[2026-03-09T00:12:02Z] billing-agent EVENT=refill_complete tenant=docusize added_tokens=250000
[2026-03-09T00:12:15Z] key=ds-prod-01 response=200 tokens_consumed=102

Observations: 429s begin before refill_start in most traces; many are clustered during the refill. Edge logs show short period where token accounting rejects requests even though refill occurs a few seconds later.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Refill race: refill occurs but accounting layer sees a transient negative window balance due to ordering between health checks and refill ledger updates.
- Burst accounting: scheduled warmups at 00:05 create burst buckets that deplete the short window immediately before refill, and our token-smoothing logic applies a protective throttle until refill finished.
- Billing sweep lock: billing agent takes a lock on tenant ledger during finalization which temporarily prevents token allocations leading to short-term 'hard' 429s.

What we've checked so far:
- Confirmed rebuild of refill ledger entries for the tenant shows refill batch writes completed within 40–120ms.
- Edge telemetry shows many short-lived streaming sessions re-establishing connections in the window causing concurrency churn.
- Replica lag on the quota read path was minimal (avg < 50ms) but spikes up to 400ms during the sweep on one replica.

Next steps planned:
- SRE to run a targeted canary of billing sweep with increased logging around ledger lock acquisition (owner: Tomás Rivera).
- Experiment: shift customer warmup schedule to 00:30 UTC for 48 hours to validate warmup/refill interaction.
- Add a temporary rule to exclude the refill maintenance window from aggressive per-route protective throttles for this tenant.
recommended_workaround:
- For immediate mitigation, ask customer to shift scheduled warmups to 00:30–01:00 UTC as a stop-gap.
- We can temporarily bump the tenant burst window (route weight) for the midnight period via a per-tenant override while we complete investigation.
- Client-side: advise exponential backoff with jitter and cap concurrent short-lived streams during maintenance windows.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Opened ticket after customer reported automated alarms at 00:12 UTC showing spike in 429s. Attached replay traces.
2026-03-10 Aisha Malik: Acknowledged. Assigning to SRE for ledger/replica checks and to Billing for sweep behavior review.
2026-03-11 Tomás Rivera (SRE): Replica lag spike noted on quota-read replica 3 between 00:09–00:13 UTC. Will instrument lock timing on next sweep run.

2026-03-11 Billing-Team-Bot: Billing sweep job v2.7 (rolled 2026-02-28) adds per-tenant reconciliation step which may briefly lock the ledger. Filing infra PR to make reconciliation non-blocking: github.com/redwood/billing/pull/72
2026-03-12 Aisha Malik: Temporarily applied tenant route-weight override for DocuSift for 00:00–01:00 UTC window to reduce 429s — monitoring metrics for two nights.
2026-03-12 Customer (DocuSift SRE): Confirmed error rate dropped after override on 2026-03-12 night. Seeking root cause patch timeline and permanent config guidance.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds applied: per-tenant midnight route-weight override and customer shifted warmups for testing.
Longer-term fix: Billing team opened PR to remove blocking ledger lock during sweep and implement asynchronous reconciliation (PR #72). SRE to add guard in rate-limiter to allow transient requests to pass if a refill is in progress and refill write timestamp is within 500ms.
Follow-ups:
- Track PR rollout and post-deploy monitor for three midnight cycles.
- Create runbook entry: 'handle-refill-contact-points' describing how to triage similar midnight refills and recommended customer warmup scheduling.
- Customer success to coordinate timeline with DocuSift; SRE to confirm when non-blocking billing sweep is live.
